subject: Aligning staged term commitments, auto-renew carveouts, and TFC
body:
From: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@brightline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@brightline.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 08:15 -0700
Subject: MSA/Order Form term questions — pilot vs committed scopes

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the redline. A few quick asks from procurement before we loop legal:
- Can Brightline get a 90-day opt-out (no cause) for pilot SKUs and non-production connectors? We want to avoid a full 12-month auto-renew for pilot work.
- For the committed Order Form we understand a 12-month minimum; however, can you add a mutual TFC (Termination for Convenience) option with a 60-day notice and a credit for prepaid months?
- For spend <$50k we want no early termination fee if we convert to a paid agreement within 6 months.

We attached your redline and our counter in-line (see Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx). Please advise if Redwood has a standard compromise matrix we can work from so legal can process quickly.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager, Brightline
Attachments: Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@brightline.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@brightline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form term questions — pilot vs committed scopes

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses and a proposed compromise: 

1) Pilot vs committed: We can accept a 90-day unilateral opt-out for pilot SKUs and explicitly non-prod environments (must be scoped in the Order Form as "Pilot SKU" or a non-production instance). For core production SKUs we need to keep the 12-month auto-renew baseline.

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC): Redwood prefers a mutual TFC rather than unilateral for committed work. Proposal: mutual TFC with 90-day notice for committed Order Forms. If Customer initiates early termination, standard approach is to apply either (a) pro-rated credits for unused prepaid months or (b) an early termination charge equal to the lesser of remaining committed fees and a 10% termination charge — whichever protects both parties.

3) Low-dollar pilots (< $50k): we can waive the early termination charge if the customer converts to a paid agreement within 6 months, provided there were no abuse patterns (eg repeated churn).

Action items: 
- Karthik / Marissa, can legal draft two short addendum options (A: mutual TFC w/90d notice + pro-rated credits; B: mutual TFC w/90d + 10% ET charge) so procurement can pick?
- Samantha, we'll produce a clean Order Form variant that flags pilot SKUs in Annex A.

If that sounds reasonable I'll ask Legal to push a redline back by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 14:20 -0700
Subject: Internal: Brightline negotiation — TFC/auto-renew playbook

Karthik / Marissa — internal sync. Samantha at Brightline pushed for a 90-day opt-out across the board and a mutual TFC with 60-day notice + credits. Proposed compromise above (pilot opt-out allowed; production = 12m baseline; mutual TFC with 90d).

Please see quick ask list below: 
- Draft two clean addendum templates (A/B) as described; make them small, procurement-friendly (one paragraph each) so procurement can choose without a full MSA rework.
- Add explicit language around what constitutes a "Pilot SKU" and ensure billing/proration rules are clear (monthly invoicing; credits applied to next invoice).
- Confirm the revenue recognition / billing team is OK with the < $50k waiver language — if we waive ET in those cases we need to lock a conversion clause (convert within 6 months or waiver void).
- Legal: prefer mutual TFC. If Legal strongly prefers unilateral, we need a pricing concession in the Order Form.

Attachments: Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx; OrderForm_Brightline_v2.pdf

Can you each confirm who will draft (A/B) and an ETA? I'd like to present options to procurement tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ben

---
From: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@brightline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@brightline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12 16:20 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form term questions — pilot vs committed scopes

Ben — this is helpful, thanks. Brightline will accept the pilot carve-out + 12-month production baseline and the mutual TFC with 90-day notice (option A preferred). A couple of follow-ups: 
- Please include explicit billing language for pro-rated credits and whether credits are refundable vs applied to future invoices. Our procurement prefers a refund for pre-paid annual fees — if refund isn't possible we need auto-apply-with-expiry (12 months).
- We'll need the addendum and a clean Order Form with pilot SKU annotations for legal review.
- Please route the final package via DocuSign and include a HubSpot deal update when it's out.

If you can share the addendum drafts and the clean OF by tomorrow EOD we'll start internal legal review.

Best,
Samantha
Sr. Procurement Manager, Brightline

Attachments referenced: Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx (see comments)
